catalog_quote: ... accento della parola con quello della frase . Nel dialetto nefusi si colgono alcuni aspetti e leggi che probabilmente permettono una certa sistematizzazione di tale questione, soprattutto facendo riferimento, tra le varie teorie dell'accento, ai principi indicati da Jespersen . L'accento è determinato dal peso della sillaba (fattori fonetici) . Se la sillaba è pesante (presenza di due consonanti o di una vocale lunga), allora si ha l'accento . Vi è una serie di parole, laddove l'accento è costante, qualunque sia la combinazione di frasi in cui vengono a trovarsi . In particolare: con parole terminanti in sillaba doppiamente chiusa, del tipo consonante + vocale breve + due consonanti, o consonante + vocale lunga + 2 consonanti, l'accento cade su questa sillaba . new_statements.quote: Fr. Beguinot consacre dans sa grammaire du berbère de Fassato un chapitre à l’accent (Il Berbero Nefûsi di Fassâto, Rome, 1924, pp. 11-14) : il y distingue des « facteurs traditionnels » conditionnés par la structure syllabique (terkéft « caravane », mais lemdînet « ville ; amoqrân « le grand », pl. imoqrânen) des « facteurs psychologiques » marquant l’insistance sur un élément particulier de la phrase [...] (uššén « chacal », mais yemlās uššen « le chacal lui dit ») et des « facteurs physiologiques » déterminant la place de l’accent lors de la composition de mots (udém figure », mais udménnes « sa figure »). [...] mais dans l’ensemble la place de l’accent est bien déterminée en berbère nefousi. La prononciation tésubla « alène » est sentie « incorrecte », seule tesublá est admise.
new_statements.translation: Fr. Beguinot devotes a chapter of his grammar of the Berber of Fassato to accent (pp. 11-14): he distinguishes 'traditional factors' conditioned by syllable structure (terkeft 'caravan' [final accent] but lemdinet 'town' [penult]; amoqran 'the big one', pl. imoqranen) from 'psychological factors' marking insistence on a particular element of the sentence (ussen 'jackal', but yemlas ussen 'the jackal said to him') and from 'physiological factors' determining accent position in word composition (udem 'face' but udmennes 'his face'). [...] but on the whole the position of the accent is well determined in Nefusi Berber. The pronunciation tesubla 'awl' [initial accent] is felt to be 'incorrect'; only tesubla [final accent] is accepted. (Nefusi informant from Kabao, summer 1972.)
new_statements.citation: Vycichl, Werner & Salem Chaker. 1984. 'Accent' (A40). Encyclopedie berbere 1: 103-106 (par. 5, by W. Vycichl), reporting Beguinot, Il Berbero Nefusi di Fassato, ch. on accent pp. 11-14. doi:10.4000/encyclopedieberbere.813
new_statements.locator: Encyclopedie berbere 1 (1984), entry A40 'Accent', p. 104, par. 5 (OpenEdition document 813)

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: line 28 (= Encyclopedie berbere 1 (1984), A40 'Accent', par. 5, signed W. Vycichl) contains the quoted passage verbatim, diacritics included; the report's two '[..]' correctly mark omitted text ('une opposition mise en evidence ou resultant de certaines constructions' and the sentence 'Dans certains cas deux prononciations sont admises may elhalennek ?.. ou may elhalennek ?,'), and the parenthesis '(Informateur nefousi, originaire de Kabao, ete 1972)' follows as translated. Vycichl misdates the grammar 'Rome, 1924' (it is 1931, 2nd ed. 1942) but the work and pages are unambiguous. I also re-read the other held passages: Cohen's review of the 1925 Saggio in BSL 27 c.r. pp. 179-1…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Nefusi has a clearly perceptible dynamic word accent whose position in the isolated word is determined mainly by syllable structure (heavy/long-vowel or doubly-closed syllables attract it: terkéft, amoqrân final vs lemdînet, imoqrânen penult), i.e. not a single fixed syllable; on top of this the accent shifts for morphosyntactic reasons (suffixation: udém ~ udménnes; retraction by one syllable after prepositions/genitive n: uráġ ~ n úraġ; kin term with possessive rûmmu vs definite rūmmû) and for phrasal emphasis/rhythm (Cohen 1927: 'fixe que dans certains schèmes de mots; ailleurs.. changée dans la phrase pour des raisons grammaticales ou rythmiques'). Speakers have firm judgements (tesublá, not *tésubla).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing reported in the accessible summaries.
new_statements.exceptions: Free variation in some phrases (māy elḥālénnek ~ māy elḥālennek 'how are you'); grammatical accent shifts after prepositions n, di, in, s, ded, af, denneg and with postposed subjects (Brugnatelli 1986 via Schiattarella 2015: 241); possessive-suffixed kin terms rûmmu 'my brother' vs rūmmû 'the brother' (Beguinot 1942: 28-29).
new_statements.domain_note: Beguinot's 'traditional factors' concern the word in isolation (citation forms, accent-marked throughout his texts); 'psychological' and rhythmic factors operate at phrase level, and Cohen 1927 reads the system as word accent regrouped into accentual groups in connected speech. All of this is second-hand: Beguinot 1925 (Rend. Lincei) and 1931/1942 (grammar, pp. 11-18) are the primary statements and were not accessible.
new_statements.identity_note: The primary description everyone cites (Beguinot 1925/1931/1942) is of the Fassato district (Jadu and nearby Jemmari) = central Nefusi, i.e. nafu1238 proper (Glottolog 5.x nafu1238 has no sub-dialects). Vycichl's own informant datum is from Kabao (western Nefusa). Souag 2023 shows Yefren (eastern Nefusa) is Zenati-like and Wazzin differs again, so 'Nefusi' is internally heterogeneous; Zuwara and Jerba are a separate Glottolog language (tuni1262 Tunisian-Zuwara Berber) and were excluded (Mitchell 1953/2009, Gussenhoven's Zwara JIPA do not count for nafu1238).

sources.note: Par. 5 (Vycichl): Beguinot's Nefusi grammar has a chapter on accent (pp. 11-14) distinguishing 'traditional' factors conditioned by syllable structure (terkeft-final vs lemdinet-penult; amoqran vs imoqranen), 'psychological' (ussen vs yemlas ussen) and 'physiological' factors (udem vs udmennes); 'dans l'ensemble la place de l'accent est bien determinee en berbere nefousi'; Vycichl's own Kabao informant (1972): only tesubla with final accent is acceptable. No default-syllable rule stated.

sources.citation: Schiattarella, Valentina. 2015. Le berbere de Siwa : documentation, syntaxe et semantique. These de doctorat, EPHE Paris. HAL tel-01794622.
sources.note: pp. 238-242: Nefusi has an 'accent dynamique' not always on the same syllable (Beguinot 1942); cites Beguinot 1942:12 urag 'fox' vs yefku n urag 'gave to the fox' (accent retraction after prepositions n, di, in, s, ded, af, denneg per Brugnatelli 1986:64-66) and 1942:28-29 rummu 'my brother' (initial accent) vs rummu 'the brother' (final accent). Second-hand.

Tout ceci semble indiquer un accent pas tres violent en intensite.' Second-hand summary of Beguinot 1925.
